    SprintForge is an open-source, macro-free project management system that generates sophisticated Excel spreadsheets with Gantt chart capabilities and probabilistic timeline predictions. Unlike existing solutions, SprintForge prioritizes agile sprint planning, enterprise security, and multi-user collaboration with Excel as the source of truth.
  • auto-music-studio 9 2
    AI Music Platform — end-to-end prompt-to-distribution pipeline with DAW integration and VST3 plugin

Hey, I'm Frank Bria 👋

I build AI development tooling, and I've spent 20+ years helping financial institutions decide which intelligent systems are worth betting on.

By day: Manager, Financial Systems at American Express — product owner for GL reconciliation and the data layer underneath finance operations. Data governance at a scale where "mostly right" isn't an option.

By night: Building in the agentic-coding space. ralph-claude-code grew to ~9.7k stars and 700+ forks, and running it in the wild taught me where AI development is actually heading: the loop is getting commoditized. The hard, valuable problems are now upstream (what are we building, and how will we know it's right?) and downstream (can we prove it works before it ships?).

In a past life: Co-founder and executive at fintech startups, and one of the creators of bank pricing-optimization technology (Nomis Solutions, SAP/Khimetrics, Earnix, Response Analytics). Industry analyst at Tower Group (now Gartner), telling banks which analytics/ML technology actually mattered and telling vendors what banks actually needed. Director/VP roles at US Bank and Truckstop.com. Author of Seven Billion Banks on personalized banking.

What I'm Building

CodeFRAME® — Think → Build → Prove → Ship

AI agents write the code. CodeFRAME owns everything before and after.

  • Think — guided requirements discovery → PRD → dependency-aware task breakdown
  • Build — hands tasks to the coding agent you already use (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Kilocode, or a built-in agent), with stall detection, retries, and batch runs
  • Prove — PROOF9, nine verification gates where every captured failure becomes a permanent requirement future builds must satisfy
  • Ship — cf pr merge only merges when proof passes

My working thesis: code quality management starts with good requirements. You can't prove something is right if you never wrote down what "right" means.

I write about this at Code & Context — AI-assisted development, proof over review, and building production-ready systems.

pip install codeframe-ai

ralph-claude-code — autonomous dev loops for Claude Code

The project that started it all: continuous autonomous development cycles with intelligent exit detection, rate limiting, and circuit breakers. With long-running goals now native in Claude Code, the loop itself is largely solved. The open question is the one Ralph users kept running into: how do you know what the agent shipped is actually right? That's where my attention has moved — PROOF9. Start with PROOF9: Review the Statement, Not the Proof.

SheetPredict — machine learning for analysts, not ML engineers

Upload a spreadsheet, walk through eight guided stages (profiling → cleaning → feature selection → AutoML → evaluation → predictions → API deployment), with plain-language explanations at every step. Next.js + FastAPI.

On the workbench

  • Proof-native forge — what would GitHub look like if PRs were built around proof obligations instead of code diffs, and agents worked in the fast lane alongside humans?
  • Formal math knowledge layer — a declaration-centric contribution layer over Lean mathematics.

The Other Stuff

I'm a mathematician at heart (MS Mathematics, MEng in Mechanical Engineering (Systems Engineering); algebraic topology and K-theory for fun) and teach college math as an adjunct instructor. Six Sigma Black Belt, MIT COO certificate.

I'm also a composer for film and media, a photographer, and I speak German fluently plus enough Russian, French, and Italian to get into trouble.

I hosted The 6 to 7 Figures Show, a podcast on scaling consulting practices — the archive is still up, and something new is in the works.

Let's Talk

I do advisory work on AI strategy, agentic development, and technical due diligence through BSG (Bria Strategy Group).

"I build intelligent systems — and help people decide which ones to bet on."

Hi there 👋

I'm Stan, a software engineer interested in all parts of the stack, from low-level system programming and infra to web development and mobile apps.

I love building and contributing to open-source projects in my free time. I also maintain a curated list of my starred projects.

Projects

Web 🌐

  • Larafeed: A web-based feed reader for following and organizing RSS feeds.
  • Bulla: A commenting system for static websites and blogs.
  • Gongyu: A bookmark manager inspired by Shaarli.
  • Pastekey: Passkey-only, end-to-end encrypted text and file sharing.
  • Meridian: Self-hosted, end-to-end encrypted Obsidian sync.
  • Enedis: A live, street-level map of power outages reported by Enedis in France.
  • Koliko: Privacy-first usage analytics for coding agents.
  • Mullvad Relay Map: An interactive map of Mullvad VPN relays with latency estimates.
  • Vélib Pulse: A map-first view of Vélib’ Métropole availability in Paris.

These days, I like to use Cloudflare Workers, React, and Effect.

Mobile 📱

  • Netclode: A self-hosted coding agent with a native iOS client built in SwiftUI.
  • firstfm-ios: iOS client for Last.fm written with Swift and SwiftUI.

Desktop 🖥️

  • Qhostty: An experimental native Qt 6 frontend for Ghostty, built for KDE Plasma on Linux.
  • Netclode: A self-hosted coding agent with a native macOS client built in SwiftUI.
  • MacThrottle: A macOS menu bar app for monitoring thermal throttling, built with SwiftUI.

Terminal 💻

  • ncda: An ncdu-like Linux TUI for monitoring live file I/O with eBPF, built with Rust, Aya, and Ratatui.
  • fast-resume: A full-text search TUI for finding and resuming coding sessions, built with Rust, Ratatui, and Tantivy.
  • pi-extensions: A collection of TypeScript extensions for the Pi coding agent, including UI, workflow, and quality-of-life features.
  • hue-tui: A TUI to control Philips Hue lights, built with Go and Bubble Tea.
  • opencode-wakatime: An OpenCode plugin written in TypeScript to track code activity in WakaTime.
  • noclaw: A tiny autonomous AI assistant written in C, shipping as a single binary with a 324 KB memory footprint. (for the meme)

Systems and sandboxing 📦

  • Netclode: A self-hosted coding environment with sessions isolated in Kata Containers microVMs using Cloud Hypervisor.
  • Codebench: Code benchmarking platform with Go workers running inside Firecracker microVMs.
  • krowl: A distributed web crawler in Go with durable local storage, consistent-hash sharding, and WARC capture.

Home automation 🏡

  • teleinfo2mqtt-rs: Convert TeleInfo frames from a Linky meter's serial port to Home Assistant-compatible MQTT messages. I also built my own MQTT client for this.
  • hue-tui: A TUI to control Philips Hue lights, built with Go and Bubble Tea.
  • lametric-time: A Linux toolkit for recovering and provisioning a LaMetric TIME through its undocumented setup API.

Infrastructure 🔁

  • wireguard-install: WireGuard VPN installer for Linux servers.
  • openvpn-install: OpenVPN installer for Linux servers.
  • nginx-autoinstall: Compile NGINX from source with custom modules and patches on Debian and Ubuntu.
  • ansible-roles: My Ansible roles for Debian and Ubuntu.
  • awesome-lxc-lxd: A curated list of awesome LXC and LXD tools, libraries, and related projects.
  • nixos-config: My NixOS configuration files.
  • arch-linux-install: My Arch Linux installation notes.
More projects
Web and tools
  • matomo-to-umami: A Python tool to migrate analytics data from Matomo (MySQL) to Umami (PostgreSQL).
  • trakt-cli: A CLI tool for trakt.tv in Go.
  • codex-wakatime: A Codex CLI plugin written in TypeScript to track code activity in WakaTime.
Infrastructure and configuration
  • feedbin-docker: Self-host your own Feedbin RSS reader in Docker.
  • docker-pleroma: Docker image for the Pleroma federated social network.
Earlier projects
  • Tereus: Code transpiling platform (Go, ANTLR, React with Remix, NSQ).
  • palette: Extract color palette from an image with k-means and k-NN (OpenCV, scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy).
  • Soundhive: Music sharing service (NestJS, Angular, JavaFX, audio fingerprint in C++).
